projects.title: Rasterix
projects.question: How does a triangle become a pixel?
projects.summary: A software rasterizer in Java. It loads OBJ meshes, projects them with a perspective matrix, fills triangles with barycentric weights, and resolves overlap with a depth buffer. Java's BufferedImage is only used to show the finished pixels.
projects.imageAlt: A textured human head model rendered by Rasterix on a black background.
projects.milestone: v1.3.0 released for macOS, Windows and Linux.
projects.nextStep: Perspective-correct texture interpolation and a measured frame-time benchmark.
evidence: Screenshots rendered by the engine's own render() method

projects.title: QuantumSim
projects.question: How can you make quantum probability something you can explore?
projects.summary: A browser lab for hydrogen-like orbitals, a particle in a 2D box, and wave-packet tunneling. The clouds are Monte Carlo samples of |ψ|², and tunneling runs a split-step Fourier solver of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation.
projects.imageAlt: QuantumSim showing a 3d z-squared orbital as a blue and white point cloud with its control panel.
projects.milestone: Version 2.5 with a field guide that derives every equation from the code.
projects.nextStep: Host a public build and add a 3D isosurface view.
evidence: Tunneling sanity check reproduced in Node: norm 1.0000, transmission 0.0404 vs 0.0324 analytic
10 figures generated from the physics modules

projects.title: Fluid simulation
projects.question: How can a few thousand particles act like a fluid?
projects.summary: A 3D smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulation in C++ and OpenGL. Each particle estimates density from its neighbours, turns it into pressure, and feels viscosity, all through smoothing kernels.
projects.imageAlt: Thousands of blue particles spreading across the floor of the simulation box, coloured by speed.
projects.milestone: Interactive 3D SPH with 3,375 particles, live sliders and mouse stirring.
projects.nextStep: Fix the cross-platform CI build and measure density error over time.
evidence: Built locally with CMake on macOS (2026-11-06)
Frames captured from the running program
credits: Inspired by Sebastian Lague's fluid simulation video

projects.title: Orion
projects.question: Can I keep a small rocket vertical with a gimballed motor and my own flight computer?
projects.summary: A thrust-vector-controlled model rocket with a custom flight computer. Right now it exists as KiCad schematics, CAD and a design journal. Nothing has been built or flown.
projects.imageAlt: CAD model of the Orion rocket: elliptical nose cone, support rods and body tubes shown apart.
projects.milestone: Schematic sheets for power, navigation sensors and flight compute; first airframe CAD (journal, Sept 14 to 20, 2026).
projects.nextStep: Finish the schematic, start PCB layout, and model the rocket in OpenRocket.

projects.title: ATLAS radio telescope
projects.question: Can a one-metre dish I build detect the 21 cm hydrogen line?
projects.summary: A planned hydrogen-line radio telescope. Neutral hydrogen emits at 1420.4 MHz; picking that up from the Milky Way is a classic first radio astronomy project. No hardware or data yet.
projects.nextStep: Choose the feed, LNA and SDR, and document the receive chain.

projects.title: Chladni plate
projects.question: What does a standing wave on a metal plate look like?
projects.summary: A Chladni plate driven by a subwoofer and a TPA3116 amplifier, with a 3D-printed enclosure. The design, wiring and costed bill of materials are documented; it has not been built yet.
projects.imageAlt: Electrical schematic for the Chladni plate: audio input, TPA3116 amplifier board and subwoofer driver.
projects.milestone: Enclosure CAD, schematic and a CA$83 bill of materials.
projects.nextStep: Print the enclosure, assemble, and photograph the first patterns.

projects.title: Myelovar
projects.question: Which non-coding variants could plausibly matter in multiple myeloma, and why?
projects.summary: A research pipeline built for a hackathon. It filters variants to regulatory regions in myeloma cells, scores transcription factor motif disruption, links each element to a target gene, and writes a plain-English evidence chain. Research use only, not a diagnostic.
projects.imageAlt: Bar chart of how many variants survive each step of the Myelovar filtering funnel.
projects.milestone: Seven-stage pipeline with REST API, web UI and tests.
evidence: Pipeline stages s0 to s6 in source
Validation figures in repository (not independently verified)
credits: ENCODE, JASPAR, DepMap, GWAS Catalog public data

projects.title: Particle simulation
projects.question: What happens when particles only feel gravity and each other?
projects.summary: C++ and OpenGL particles with Velocity Verlet integration, inverse-square gravity, elastic collisions and a containing sphere. Builds for macOS, Linux and Windows.
projects.milestone: v1.1 release with builds for three operating systems.

projects.title: Buffy
projects.question: What would a personal assistant look like if I could read every line of it?
projects.summary: A desktop assistant in Electron and TypeScript. It runs a local model through Ollama or Claude through the API, and any file write or shell command waits for my approval. It grew out of an earlier Python voice prototype.
projects.milestone: Tool calling, approvals, calendar, memory and a phone companion page.

projects.title: Lorenz attractor
projects.question: How can a simple system become unpredictable?
projects.summary: A Python notebook that integrates the Lorenz system and plots its attractor, with notes on chaos, phase space and the Van der Pol oscillator.

projects.title: Machine learning notebooks
projects.question: What is a model actually doing when it learns?
projects.summary: Linear regression, the normal equation and logistic regression written with NumPy and pandas rather than a machine learning library.
